lines: Middle Eastern crisis Gaza war Twenty-one people are killed, 45 are injured, and about 100 others are missing after a residential building in Gaza City collapses after it was previously hit by an Israeli airstrike. (AFP via France 24) (Al Jazeera)
2026 West Kordofan mine collapse At least 70 people are reported to be killed in a gold mine explosion in Sudan's West Kordofan state. (Al Jazeera)
2026 South Korea—Central Asia summit The first summit between South Korea and the five countries of Central Asia is held in Seoul. (Euronews) (Korea Times)

Canada–European Union relations European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen invites Canada to become the first associate member of the European Union amidst the ongoing trade war between Canada and the United States. (CNBC)

North Korea–South Korea relations Inter-Korean Liaison Office bombing A district court in Seoul, South Korea, orders North Korea to pay KRW 44.6 billion (US$32.5 million) in damages for destroying the Inter-Korean Liaison Office in Kaesong in 2020, in South Korea's first damages lawsuit against North Korea. (AFP via CNA)

War crimes in the Kosovo War The Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentences former prime minister Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison after convicting him on charges of murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention committed during the Kosovo War. (AP)

Human rights in Macau Macau begins its first closed-door national security trial against former legislator Au Kam San, who faces charges including subversion of state power and alleged ties with foreign groups and media outlets. He faces up to 25 years in prison. (AFP via RTL Today)

2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election The Philippine Commission on Elections proclaims all 78 elected members of the Bangsamoro Parliament, with four parties given all seats for party representation. The Bangsamoro Federalist Party, earning most of the seats, fails to secure a majority, leading to a hung parliament. Meanwhile, six sectoral seats are given to the United Bangsamoro Justice Party. (Al Jazeera) (Manila Bulletin)

The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) announces that its finals will move to Charlotte, North Carolina, United States, from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for three years beginning in 2027, with matches at the Spectrum Center. The WTA also relocates its global headquarters from St. Petersburg, Florida, U.S., to Charlotte. (AFP)
